findings.title: No .env file committed to the repo
findings.why: Anyone with repo access (or a leak) gets your real keys and can run up your bills or read your data.
findings.verify: List tracked env files; rotate any keys that were committed.
findings.note: Env file(s) are not git-ignored; if ever committed, rotate every key inside.

findings.title: .gitignore excludes .env files
findings.why: Without it, the next `git add .` commits your secrets.
findings.note: .gitignore does not list .env files.

findings.title: No secrets hard-coded in source
findings.why: Keys in code end up in git history and, for frontend code, in every visitor's browser.
findings.verify: Grep for key patterns; rotate anything found.
findings.note: Values are hidden on purpose: open the file and line, move the value to an env var, then rotate the key.

findings.title: Every API route that changes or reveals user data checks who is calling
findings.why: An unprotected route lets anyone on the internet read or edit other users' data.
findings.verify: Read each flagged route; confirm it verifies a session/token and the owner of the record.
findings.note: 1 route(s) show no sign of an auth check. Confirm by reading each.

findings.title: Rate limiting on login, signup and expensive routes
findings.why: Bots can brute-force passwords, spam you, or burn paid API credits within hours of launch.
findings.verify: Look for a rate-limit library or provider setting.
findings.note: No rate-limiting code or library found. If your host/CDN (Cloudflare, Vercel firewall) rate-limits for you, mark PASS and say where.

findings.title: Security headers set (CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options etc.)
findings.why: Cheap protection against clickjacking, MIME sniffing and some XSS.
findings.note: No security-header setup found (host-level headers in vercel.json/netlify.toml count: check).

findings.title: CORS is not open to every origin
findings.why: A wildcard CORS policy lets any website call your API from your users' browsers.

findings.title: Debug mode is off for production
findings.why: Debug mode exposes stack traces, internal paths and sometimes an interactive console.

findings.title: User input is validated on the server
findings.why: Without validation, malformed or hostile input reaches your database and crashes things.
findings.note: No validation library found; check whether routes validate input by hand.

findings.title: Database access rules (row-level security) are enabled
findings.why: With Supabase/Firebase, the browser talks to the database directly: no rules means anyone can read everything.
findings.verify: RLS enabled + policies per table (also check the provider dashboard).
findings.note: SQL files exist but none enable row level security.

findings.title: Dependencies have no known critical vulnerabilities
findings.why: Old packages are the most common way small apps get hacked.
findings.verify: Run npm audit / pip-audit / equivalent and read the result.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Run npm audit / pip-audit / equivalent and read the result.

findings.title: Server-only keys are not exposed to the browser
findings.why: Variables prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/REACT_APP_ are shipped to every visitor.
findings.verify: Look for secret-looking names in public env vars.
findings.note: A server-style secret is exposed through a public (browser) env variable.

findings.title: Payment webhooks verify the signature
findings.why: Without it anyone can POST a fake 'payment succeeded' and get your product free.
findings.verify: constructEvent / construct_event in the webhook handler.
findings.note: Webhook handler has no signature verification.

findings.title: Webhook handling is idempotent (same event twice = one effect)
findings.why: Payment providers retry; duplicates can double-grant credits or double-send emails.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Event ids stored/checked before acting.

findings.title: Paid features are enforced on the server, not only hidden in the UI
findings.why: Hiding a button is not access control: free users can call the API directly.
findings.verify: Read paid-feature routes for a plan/subscription check.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Read paid-feature routes for a plan/subscription check.

findings.title: Failed payment and cancellation paths exist
findings.why: Cards fail and customers cancel every week. Without handling, access and billing drift apart.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Handlers for invoice.payment_failed / subscription.deleted.

findings.title: Live-mode keys and webhook secret configured for production (not test keys)
findings.why: Test keys in production mean you take no real money; live keys in dev risk real charges.
findings.verify: Check hosting env vars and provider dashboard.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Check hosting env vars and provider dashboard.

findings.title: Automatic database backups are on and a restore was tried
findings.why: One bad migration or deleted table can end the business without a backup you've actually restored.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Provider dashboard: backups/PITR.

findings.title: Database schema changes are tracked as migrations
findings.why: Hand-edited production databases drift and can't be rebuilt or rolled back.
findings.verify: migrations dir / prisma migrate / alembic / supabase/migrations

findings.title: Users can delete their account/data
findings.why: Privacy laws (GDPR/CCPA) expect it, and users ask within weeks.
findings.note: No delete-account flow found.

findings.title: Errors are reported to a tracker (Sentry or similar)
findings.why: Without it you learn about crashes from angry users, if at all.
findings.note: No error-tracking SDK found.

findings.title: A health-check endpoint exists
findings.why: Uptime monitors and hosts need one URL that says 'I'm alive'.
findings.note: No /health-style route detected.

findings.title: Automated tests exist for the critical paths
findings.why: Without tests, every AI edit after launch can silently break signup or payment.
findings.note: No test files or runner found.

findings.title: A CI pipeline runs build/tests on every push
findings.why: Catches broken builds before users do.
findings.note: No .github/workflows. (GitLab/CircleCI users: mark PASS with the file.)

findings.title: A dependency lockfile is committed
findings.why: Without it, production can install different versions than you tested.

findings.title: Friendly 404 and error pages
findings.why: A raw stack trace or blank page at launch looks broken and leaks details.
findings.note: No custom 404/error page found.

findings.title: Outbound calls (APIs, AI, email) have timeouts and failure handling
findings.why: One slow third party can hang every request or crash the server.
findings.verify: Read the code around external calls.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Read the code around external calls.

findings.title: Privacy policy page exists
findings.why: Required in most places once you collect emails or use analytics; payment/ad providers require it.
findings.note: No privacy-policy page found. Template only; have a professional review.

findings.title: Terms of service page exists
findings.why: Sets the rules for use, refunds and liability; expected by payment providers.
findings.note: No terms page found.

findings.title: Cookie/analytics consent where required
findings.why: Analytics or ad cookies without consent can breach EU/UK rules.
findings.note: No analytics/ad trackers detected.

findings.title: Refund/cancellation policy is stated (if charging money)
findings.why: Disputes and chargebacks follow when buyers can't find the rules.
findings.note: No refund/cancellation policy found.

findings.title: Pages have a title, description and social preview tags
findings.why: This is what Google and link previews show; blank means nobody clicks.
findings.note: Missing: title/description, Open Graph/social tags.

findings.title: robots.txt and sitemap exist
findings.why: Helps search engines find and index the right pages.
findings.note: Missing: robots.txt, sitemap.

findings.title: Images have alt text
findings.why: Screen-reader users and SEO both rely on it.
findings.note: 1 file(s) have without alt.

findings.title: No oversized images/assets shipped
findings.why: A multi-megabyte image makes the first visit slow on mobile.

findings.title: An .env.example documents required variables
findings.why: The next person (or you in 3 months) can't deploy without guessing.
findings.note: Code reads 3 env var(s) but no .env.example documents them.

findings.title: README explains how to run and deploy
findings.why: Future you and any helper need it.
findings.note: README has no run/deploy instructions.

findings.title: Password reset and email verification work (or a managed provider handles them)
findings.why: Users who forget a password become support tickets or lost customers; unverified emails enable abuse.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Provider (Clerk/Auth0/Supabase) or custom reset flow.

findings.title: Sending domain has SPF, DKIM and DMARC
findings.why: Otherwise your signup and receipt emails land in spam.
findings.verify: DNS records for the sending domain.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: DNS records for the sending domain.

findings.title: You can roll back a bad deploy
findings.why: The first bad release will happen; you need a way back in minutes.
findings.note: Cannot be judged from code alone: Host rollback feature / tagged releases.
